sources.entry: Clipboard - An easy-to-use clipboard manager with time saving features that work across all terminals.

summary.one_liner: Clipboard (cb) is a cross-platform command-line clipboard manager that stores files, directories, and raw data in numbered or persistent clipboards with history, notes, regex-based ignore rules, and scripting support.
summary.what_it_does: The tool provides a single "cb" command for copying, cutting, pasting, adding, removing, showing, searching, and clearing items across multiple named clipboards (temporary numbered ones or persistent ones named with a suffix like _420). Each clipboard keeps a history that can be browsed, reordered, cleared by range, and exported or imported as folders. Piped input and output work with ordinary shell commands, and regex patterns select items for removal or search. Ignore rules, optionally hashed secrets, and a "cut" action that deletes content after pasting are included for sensitive data. Behavior is configurable through environment variables for temp and persist directories, history size limits, locale, color themes, and an option to run user scripts before or after actions. The README also describes integration with GUI clipboard systems, which can be disabled.
use_cases: copy files from the terminal and paste them elsewhere
keep multiple persistent clipboards across sessions
pipe command output into a clipboard and paste it later
share clipboard contents between shell scripts
store and auto-delete a one-time password or secret
search and manage clipboard history from the command line
how_to_run: git clone the repository, then cd Clipboard/build
stack: X11 or Wayland (optional GUI clipboard support)
notable: Named temporary and persistent clipboards, each with its own history and notes
Regex-based search, removal, and ignore rules, plus hashed secret ignoring
Cut action that deletes content after it is pasted
Scripts that run before or after chosen actions, with environment variables exposed
Configurable history limit by size or age and multiple color themes
caveats: The README asks for a C++ developer to help because development cannot continue without one.
Building from source requires CMake, C++20, OpenSSL, and on Linux ALSA plus X11 or Wayland libraries for GUI integration.
Export and import currently use a fixed folder name, Exported_Clipboards.
